values.description: In the level, but not yet triggered. Its control routine does not run.
values.name: INACTIVE

values.description: Triggered: its control routine runs every frame.
values.name: ACTIVE

values.description: Ran and finished - a creature that died, or a one-shot trigger that fired. It stays in the level, but no longer runs.
values.name: DEACTIVATED

values.description: Neither drawn nor collidable, as a pickup Lara has already collected is.
values.name: INVISIBLE

functions.description: Retrieves an item by 1-based index or by name.
examples:
local item = trx.items[1]
item.name = "lara"
local lara = trx.items["lara"]

params.description: 1-based index, or the item's unique name.
params.name: key

functions.description: Creates a new item of the given object type at the given position.
examples:
local wolf = trx.items.spawn(
  trx.catalog.objects.wolf, trx.lara.item.pos, 0, { activate = true })

params.description: World position. Must lie inside the level.
params.name: pos

params.description: `activate`: bring the item to life, enabling AI for creatures.
params.name: opts

returns.description: `nil` if the item pool is exhausted.

functions.description: Returns the total number of allocated items. Same as `#trx.items`.
Finds all items matching the query.

params.description: Supported keys: `object_id`, `room_num`. Unknown keys are ignored and logged.
params.name: query

functions.description: Finds the first item matching the query.

types.description: An item, also known as a moveable.

extensions.description: Typed, object-specific item properties. Writing here overrides the object's default for this item only; reads fall back to the object. Iterable with `pairs()`. See [Objects](../../OBJECTS.md).
extensions.name: properties

fields.description: Object-relative animation number, 0-indexed.
fields.name: anim

fields.description: Current animation state.
fields.name: anim_state

fields.description: Whether Lara can collide with this item.
fields.name: collidable

fields.description: Vertical speed.
fields.name: fall_speed

fields.description: Trigger-related flag bits. Read-only: writing them directly would let a script set `IF_KILLED` without unlinking the item, wedging engine state. Use `kill()` instead.
fields.name: flags

fields.description: Object-relative frame number, 0-indexed. Negative values count back from the end.
fields.name: frame

fields.description: Animation state the item is transitioning towards.
fields.name: goal_anim_state

fields.description: Whether gravity applies to this item.
fields.name: gravity

fields.description: Current hit points. Raising this above the maximum also raises `properties.max_hit_points`.
fields.name: hit_points

fields.description: Whether the item's control routine is running. Call `activate()` to start it.
fields.name: is_active

fields.description: Whether the item is a living creature with hit points remaining.
fields.name: is_alive

fields.description: Whether this item is a creature currently hostile to Lara.
fields.name: is_hostile

fields.description: Whether the item has already been killed.
fields.name: is_killed

fields.description: Maximum hit points. Set `properties.max_hit_points` to change it.
fields.name: max_hit_points

fields.description: Bitmask of which of the item's meshes are drawn.
fields.name: mesh_bits

fields.description: Unique item name, or `nil`. Assigning a name already in use raises an error.
fields.name: name

fields.description: The item's object type.
fields.name: object_id

fields.description: World position. Updating this also updates `room` and `room_num`.
fields.name: pos

fields.description: 1-based number of the room containing this item. Set `pos` to move the item between rooms.
fields.name: room_num

fields.description: Orientation.
fields.name: rot

fields.description: Forward speed.
fields.name: speed

fields.description: Item status. Use `activate()` and `kill()` to change it, so the item's active-list membership stays in sync.
fields.name: status

fields.description: Trigger-related timer value.
fields.name: timer

fields.description: Bitmask of which of the item's meshes Lara is touching.
fields.name: touch_bits

fields.description: Whether the item was hit during the current frame.
fields.name: was_hit

methods.description: Adds the item to the active list and starts its control routine. Objects with no control routine cannot be activated.
methods.name: activate

methods.description: Distance from this item to a world position.
methods.name: distance_to

methods.description: Runs the object's death handling with an explosion, as a rocket or a grenade would. Unlike `kill()`, which simply removes the item from the game.
methods.name: explode

methods.description: Reads an object property, falling back to the object's default. Prefer `item.properties.<name>`.
methods.name: get_property

methods.description: Names of every property this item's object declares.
methods.name: get_property_names

methods.description: Whether the handle still refers to a live item. Reading or writing a field on a stale handle raises an error rather than silently operating on an unrelated item, so check this for a handle held across time.
examples:
local wolf = trx.items.first({ object_id = trx.catalog.objects.wolf })
trx.events.after_control(function()
  if wolf:is_valid() and wolf.hit_points <= 0 then
    trx.log.info("the wolf is down")
  end
end)
methods.name: is_valid

methods.description: Removes the item from the game. Any other handle to it becomes stale.
methods.name: kill

methods.description: Overrides an object property for this item. Prefer `item.properties.<name> = ...`.
methods.name: set_property
